notes.note: Wax plant is a climber that also suits a hanging basket. Through the growing season, water moderately and consistently, letting the soil get nearly dry in between. In winter, the plant needs less water and less bright light. It loves high humidity, so try a humidifier or set the pot on a tray of wet pebbles. Use a loose, fast-draining mix rich in organic matter and a pot with good drainage. Soil kept too wet or too dry can make the leaves drop.

notes.note: Grow prayer plant indoors in bright light, away from strong direct sun. Too much sun will fade the colors of its leaves. Keep the soil evenly moist through the growing season, then water less so it dries out in winter. The plant needs high humidity, so keep it in a humidified room or on a tray of wet pebbles. Pot it in a soil-based potting mix. Feed it monthly in the growing season, then feed much less from autumn to late winter.

notes.note: Set your Chinese money plant near a north, east, or west window. In a south-facing room, set it back from the window so it gets no direct sun. Keep it out of cold drafts and always above 50°F. Water when the top few centimeters of soil start drying, checking with a finger or by lifting the pot. From April to September, you can feed every 1 to 2 months with balanced liquid fertilizer at label strength.

notes.note: Bachelor's button is a cool-weather annual grown in average, well-drained soil. Plant it in beds, borders, cottage gardens, meadows, or a cutting garden. Give it full sun to light shade, since too much shade makes the stems flop. It prefers moderately moist soil but copes with little water. Avoid spots that stay wet. It tolerates poor soil and needs little or no fertilizer.

notes.note: Nasturtium is a warm-season annual with long stems and parasol-like leaves, grown in many kinds of gardens. Climbing types can quickly cover a fence or trellis. Choose a spot in full sun, with some afternoon shade when summers run hot. It tolerates drought. Plant it in poor, well-drained soil, since overly rich soil brings leaves at the expense of flowers. Fertilizer also adds leaves but cuts down on flowering.
